llmThreads.title: LLM threads

The limit is the sum of each Base URL's concurrency; new sessions are balanced evenly across endpoints and, once full, queued in arrival order. Endpoints with an exhausted quota are not picked even while idle. Manage the model pool on the Settings page.

recon.label: Recon
recon.hint: Maps the project structure and auth, fills in source extensions, collects historical vulns, and weights files for later mining.

code_intel.label: Code graph
code_intel.hint: Optional. CodeGraph builds a code database for src/ so the Worker / Reviewer can query call relations. Off by default to save disk; when on it runs alongside recon and mining waits for both. On failure it degrades to Read/Grep.

worker.label: Mining
worker.hint: After recon, mines file by file; if the code graph is on it also waits for that build. Lite mode injects only weight-100 entry points. Fast scan traces back from Semgrep sinks. Historical-vuln bypass tries each doc in turn. Unconstrained scan injects only the map and auth with a single fixed Worker, ending once the Reviewer judges front-facing RCE impact. Mining is complete only after every enabled path finishes.

reviewer.label: Review
reviewer.hint: Independently verifies the vulnerabilities the Worker submits. Static review only by default; live-lab mode runs an HTTP PoC first, local verification uses a sandbox harness.

verifier.label: Verify
verifier.hint: Optional. After the Reviewer confirms a front-facing vulnerability, uses FOFA to search for matching targets; it first understands the exploit from the report and PoC, runs the original PoC where possible, and builds a payload from the report when none is usable. On failure it adjusts the exploit on the same chain and retries. 10 targets per round by default, stopping after 3 successes; otherwise it searches the next round, up to 5 rounds / 50 targets.

attack_chain.label: Attack chain
attack_chain.hint: Optional. After mining and review finish, tries multi-step chained exploitation of confirmed vulnerabilities to widen impact; skipped when fewer than 2 are confirmed.

done.label: Done
done.hint: Recon, mining, review and (if enabled) online verification / attack-chain linking have all finished.

branchHint.map: Maps modules, HTTP and non-HTTP entry points and the tech stack, and writes the login / roles / permissions docs.
branchHint.source_ext: Adds execution-surface files not indexed by default (templates, ORM mappings, etc.) to the index.
branchHint.old_vulns: First runs the GHSA and GitHub Issues crawlers and the Agent saves the results; then uses WebSearch to fill gaps.
branchHint.mark: Weights or skips source files in batches, setting mining priority.
branchHint.lab: Uses Docker to build a reusable default lab for dynamic reproduction; not to manufacture exploit conditions.
branchHint.manualLab: Uses the user-provided vulnerable environment for dynamic verification, skipping the Docker build.
branchHint.harness: Extracts the function and mocks dependencies to run a harness in a sandbox; no full-project lab.

workerHint.mine: After recon, files are weighted: entry points are mined forward, lower weights are traced back by role or control surface. If the code graph is on it also waits for that build. Missing auth, IDOR and business logic rely on this path.
workerHint.fast: Semgrep finds sinks and each is traced back. Runs in parallel with heuristic mining, covering SAST sinks.
workerHint.bypass: After historical-vuln collection, tries each doc in turn to bypass the patch or confirm an unfixed bug is still exploitable.
workerHint.unconstrained: Starts after recon, injecting only the code map and auth. If the code graph is on it also waits for that build. Always uses the bounty gate; ends once the Reviewer judges front-facing RCE impact.

auditFlow.ariaLabel: Audit flow for the current selection
auditFlow.heading: Audit flow for the current selection
auditFlow.footer: After historical-vuln collection, heuristic mining, historical-vuln bypass and unconstrained scan can run alongside file weighting; fast scan waits for all four recon steps. Enabled mining paths run in parallel and alongside review: mining and review happen at the same time. Obvious false positives are dropped this round; the Reviewer fixes and confirms PoC and report packaging; a finding is returned to Fix only when the root-cause analysis was wrong. The project completes only after every enabled mining path finishes.

bounty.label: High-impact only
bounty.hint: RCE, injection, arbitrary file operations, broken access control, stored XSS, 1-click CSRF, hardcoded secrets with server-side impact, etc.

full.label: Includes low-impact
full.hint: CORS, reflected XSS, missing rate limiting, security headers, etc., tiered by the Reviewer.

unconstrained.hint: This path always uses the bounty gate, regardless of the project's full / custom mode.

recon.title: Recon
recon.body: Maps structure and auth, fills in extensions, collects historical vulns and weights files. Heuristic mining, historical-vuln bypass and unconstrained scan start after historical-vuln collection; fast scan waits for all four steps (weighting included).
recon.hint: Recon runs first after import: code map, source extensions, historical vulns, file weighting. Heuristic mining does not wait for all weighting to finish.

body.liteBounty: Focuses only on weight-100 entry points (HTTP / WebSocket / RPC / MQ), forward source→sink. Missing auth, IDOR and business logic rely on this. Records only high-impact bugs exploitable by default.
body.liteFull: Focuses only on weight-100 entry points (HTTP / WebSocket / RPC / MQ), forward source→sink. Missing auth, IDOR and business logic rely on this. Also records low-impact items like CORS and reflected XSS.
body.fullBounty: File weighting: entry points mined forward, Service / filters traced back or by control surface, low weights lightly scanned. Missing auth, IDOR and business logic rely on this. Records only high-impact bugs exploitable by default.
body.fullFull: File weighting: entry points mined forward, Service / filters traced back or by control surface, low weights lightly scanned. Missing auth, IDOR and business logic rely on this. Also records low-impact items like CORS and reflected XSS.

hint.lite: After historical-vuln collection, the heuristic Worker injects only weight-100 unaudited files; lower weights are not entry points and do not block completion. Can run alongside file weighting.
hint.full: After historical-vuln collection, the heuristic Worker mines high-weight unaudited files; can run alongside file weighting. Enabled mining paths run in parallel and mining completes only after all finish.

fast.title: Fast scan

body.Bounty: Semgrep finds sinks; after a code filter and an Agent filter, each is traced back. Covers SAST sinks; missing auth / IDOR / business logic are out of scope. High-impact only.
body.Full: Semgrep finds sinks; after a code filter and an Agent filter, each is traced back. Covers SAST sinks; missing auth / IDOR / business logic are out of scope. Also records low-impact items.

fast.hint: After recon: Semgrep → code filter → sink triage → Fast Worker traces back each; runs alongside heuristic mining.

bypass.title: Historical-vuln bypass

body.Bounty: Takes historical-vuln docs as input; each round tries to bypass one patch or confirm an unfixed bug is still exploitable. Records only high-impact bugs exploitable by default.
body.Full: Takes historical-vuln docs as input; each round tries to bypass one patch or confirm an unfixed bug is still exploitable. Also records low-impact items.

bypass.hint: After historical-vuln collection, injects each doc in turn; runs alongside heuristic / fast scan.

unconstrained.title: Unconstrained scan
unconstrained.body: Injects only the code map and auth, dispatching no weighted files. A single fixed Worker, always on the bounty gate. The path ends once the Reviewer judges a front-facing bug to have achieved RCE impact; other front-facing bugs are still submitted.
unconstrained.hint: Starts after historical-vuln collection, isolated from heuristic mining. The end condition is the Reviewer's judgment of RCE impact, not vuln_type.

codeIntel.title: Code graph
codeIntel.bodyOn: Runs alongside recon. CodeGraph builds a call graph for src/ so the Worker / Reviewer can query relations. On failure it degrades to Read/Grep.
codeIntel.bodyOff: Off. No code database; mining just waits for recon, and the Worker / Reviewer use Read / Grep.
codeIntel.hintOn: The index is written to src/.codegraph/ and can be large. Source changes only mark it stale; the user triggers a rebuild.
codeIntel.hintOff: Off by default so not every project builds a graph and uses disk. When checked it runs alongside recon and mining waits for both.
codeIntel.chipSrcHint: Does not index jar/class, leaving those for a later Jar Analyzer.

body.lab: An isolated-environment round builds a Docker lab. The Reviewer fixes the PoC and reproduces it; do not return it to the Worker to fix the PoC.
body.labManual: Prefers your provided lab, falling back to Docker if unreachable. The Reviewer fixes the PoC and reproduces it; do not return it to the Worker to fix the PoC.
body.harness: No full-project lab. The Reviewer extracts the function, mocks dependencies, and runs a harness in a sandbox; a successful run is recorded as local verification.
body.static: Static review only. If default exploitability can be proven, it is recorded as static_only with no lab.

hint.lab: With live-lab mode on, the Reviewer builds the lab and closes out the HTTP PoC; debug MCP is used only when the PoC is unusable and needs rewriting. The lab provides only the default deployment.
hint.harness: Local verification and live-lab mode are mutually exclusive. No Docker or a failed mock does not cause a false positive.
hint.static: Dynamic verification off by default. When static evidence already proves default exploitability, the finding is recorded directly with no Docker.

chip.manualLabHint: Review prefers the manual lab address; falls back to a Docker lab if unreachable.
chip.pocHint: Runs the current HTTP PoC and container logs first. The Reviewer fixes the PoC until it reproduces; Java / Node / Python debug MCP is used only when it is missing, won't run, or fails and needs rewriting. Do not return it to the Worker to fix the PoC.
chip.harnessHint: RunCode executes in a one-shot sibling container; the script is written to harness.py. Do not copy mocks into poc.py; a pure library bug with no install surface may skip poc.py.
chip.staticHint: No lab; sufficient static evidence is enough to confirm and record.

verifier.title: Verify
verifier.bodyOn: After the Reviewer confirms a front-facing vulnerability, uses FOFA to search for matching targets; it first understands the exploit from the report and PoC, runs the original PoC where possible, and builds a payload from the report when none is usable. On failure it adjusts the exploit on the same chain and retries. 10 targets by default, stopping after 3 successes.
verifier.bodyOff: Off. No internet targets are searched after confirmation.
verifier.hintOn: When this batch of 10 falls short of 3 successes, it keeps the successes and searches the next round, up to 5 rounds (50 targets total). A matching query is shared within the project. Destructive bugs (arbitrary file deletion, DoS, SQL writes, etc.) are skipped. Requires a FOFA key.
verifier.hintOff: Online verification off by default. Only when checked does it run a FOFA re-test after confirming a front-facing vulnerability.

chip.frontendHint: Admin-panel bugs do not go through online re-testing.
chip.threeHint: Each round of 10 ends after 3 successes; otherwise it keeps the successes and searches the next round, up to 5 rounds / 50 targets.
chip.skipHint: Bugs that would disrupt a live service (arbitrary file deletion, DoS, SQL writes, etc.) are skipped automatically.

attackChain.title: Attack chain
attackChain.bodyOn: After mining and review finish, tries multi-step chained exploitation of confirmed vulnerabilities to widen impact.
attackChain.bodyOff: Off. No attack-chain linking after review.
attackChain.hintOn: Considers only this project's confirmed output; skipped when fewer than 2 are confirmed. With a Docker lab, non-interactive chains are dynamically verified and the script saved; chains that need interaction (XSS, etc.) skip verification.
attackChain.hintOff: Attack-chain linking off by default. Only when checked does it try multi-bug linking after both mining and review finish.

chip.confirmedHint: pending / false positive / merged sub-items do not participate.
chip.min2Hint: Skipped when fewer than 2 confirmed bugs, so the LLM does not run for nothing.

done.title: Done
done.body: Recon, mining and review are finished, and the vulnerability report is produced.
done.bodyWithPost: Recon, mining, review and the enabled post stages are all finished, and the vulnerability report is produced.
done.hint: The pipeline is done. You can still change dynamic verification, online verification, attack-chain linking or the code graph in project settings, or reset mining progress and resume in a different mode.

attackChain.label: Attack-chain linking
attackChain.hint: After both mining and review finish, tries multi-step chained exploitation of this project's confirmed vulnerabilities to widen the impact. Skipped automatically when fewer than 2 vulnerabilities are confirmed. When a local Docker lab exists, writes a chaining script and dynamically verifies chains that need no user interaction; chains that require interaction (XSS, etc.) skip verification. Off by default.

verifier.label: Verifier (online verification)
verifier.hint: After the Reviewer confirms a front-facing vulnerability, uses FOFA to search for matching internet targets. It first understands the exploit from the report and PoC and runs the original PoC where possible; when no usable HTTP PoC exists it builds a payload from the report rather than skipping; if that fails it adjusts the exploit on the same finding and retries. By default it searches 10 targets per round and stops after 3 successes; otherwise it keeps the successes and searches the next round, up to 5 rounds (50 targets total). Vulnerabilities that would disrupt or tamper with a live service (arbitrary file deletion, DoS, SQL writes, etc.) are only tested after you confirm. Requires a FOFA key in Settings. Off by default.

codeIntel.label: Build call graph
codeIntel.hint: Runs alongside recon. When checked, CodeGraph builds a call graph for src/ so the Worker / Reviewer can look up symbols and calls. The index is written to src/.codegraph/ and rebuilds overwrite the same directory. Failure degrades gracefully and does not block the audit. Off by default to save disk; if enabled mid-run, mining waits for this build to finish. Disabling it deletes this project's index.

off.label: Off
off.hint: The Reviewer does static review only; confirmations use static_only. Default option.

lab.label: Live lab
lab.hint: An isolated-environment round builds a Docker lab (or you provide a manual lab) and reproduces the bug with an HTTP PoC / debug MCP. Evidence level dynamic / mcp.

harness.label: Local verification
harness.hint: No full-project lab. The Reviewer extracts the function, mocks dependencies, and runs a harness in a Docker sandbox. A successful run is recorded as local verification, distinct from a live lab. Falls back to static when Docker is unavailable.

heuristic.label: Heuristic mining
heuristic.hint: After historical-vuln collection finishes, files are weighted and the Worker mines source→sink from high-weight unaudited files. Missing auth, IDOR and business-logic bugs still rely on this path.

lite.label: Lite
lite.hint: Uses only weight-100 files as entry points; lower weights do not block completion. Off by default, which audits every weighted file.

fast.label: Fast scan
fast.hint: After recon, Semgrep matches sinks; a hard code filter then an Agent freezes about 60, and the Fast Worker traces back from each sink. Covers SAST sinks; does not replace heuristic mining.

bypass.label: Historical-vuln bypass
bypass.hint: After historical-vuln collection finishes, each round injects one historical-vuln document and tries to bypass the patch, produce a variant, or confirm an unfixed bug is still exploitable.

unconstrained.label: Unconstrained scan
unconstrained.hint: Starts after historical-vuln collection with a single fixed Worker. Injects only the code map and auth document, dispatching no weighted files. Always uses the bounty gate; the path ends once the Reviewer judges a front-facing bug to have achieved RCE-level impact.

manualLab.label: Manual lab
manualLab.hint: For vulnerability environments that must be set up by hand. Once you fill in the address, credentials and other details, review uses this description first and only falls back to a Docker lab if it is unreachable. You can also add it later in project settings; it takes effect on the next review round.
manualLab.placeholder: e.g. lab at http://127.0.0.1:8080, credentials admin/admin, login at /login. You can also add paths, auth headers, etc.

reconHint.label: Recon hint
reconHint.hint: Optional. Paste text or upload a .txt / .md file as an extra manual hint injected into each recon sub-stage (map/auth, extensions, historical vulns, marking). Do not use it to skip gate tasks; editable while running, effective next round.
reconHint.placeholder: e.g. focus on SSO and admin-panel routes; ignore demo modules; treat the JWT filter as the source of truth for auth.
reconHint.tooLong: Recon hint is too long; max {{max}} characters

workerHint.label: Mining Worker hint
workerHint.hint: Optional. Paste text or upload a .txt / .md file as an extra manual hint injected into every mining round of heuristic, fast scan, historical-vuln bypass and unconstrained scan. Do not use it to shift focus; editable while running, effective next round.
workerHint.placeholder: e.g. focus on admin-panel export and file download; ignore demo accounts; treat the JWT filter as the source of truth for auth.
workerHint.tooLong: Mining hint is too long; max {{max}} characters

hintText.uploadTextFile: Please upload a .txt or .md text file

attackSurfaceBadge.frontend: Front-facing vulnerability: reachable publicly or without logging in.
attackSurfaceBadge.backendAdmin: Admin-panel vulnerability: requires admin privileges to exploit.
attackSurfaceBadge.backendUser: Admin-panel vulnerability: requires an ordinary in-app account (low-privilege user) to exploit.
attackSurfaceBadge.backend: Admin-panel vulnerability: requires a suitable in-app account to exploit.

vulnTags.subItemTip: A sub-report within a merged same-root-cause group; see the main report or expand the group for details.
vulnTags.tierTip: {{tier}}: value tier assigned when the Reviewer confirmed it.
vulnTags.verifierTip: Verifier online re-test status. See the vulnerability details for the full target list.

miningTooltip.heuristic: Produced by the heuristic Worker mining file by file after recon completes.
miningTooltip.fast: Produced by the fast-scan path (Semgrep → SinkTriage → Fast Worker).
miningTooltip.bypass: Produced by the historical-vuln bypass path attempting patch bypass or confirming an unfixed bug.
miningTooltip.unconstrained: Produced by the unconstrained-scan path. This path always uses the bounty gate; the Reviewer judges whether RCE-level impact was achieved.

configTip.specific: Only triggerable after changing the application's own config options; excludes risk toggles the vendor already warns about.

trackingTip.submitted: You marked this as submitted externally.
trackingTip.ignored: You marked this as ignored; no further submission follow-up.

bounty.label: Bounty mode
bounty.short: Only high-impact bugs exploitable by default
bounty.hint: Records only high-impact classes exploitable by default (RCE, injection, arbitrary file operations, broken access control, stored XSS, 1-click CSRF, source-code hardcoded secrets with server-side impact, etc.). Low-impact items such as CORS, reflected XSS, plain CSRF and missing rate limiting are not recorded; user-changeable passwords in config files and front-end transport-obfuscation AES / publicly shipped keys do not count. Exploitation must hold under the default config or the application's own config options; mark each submission as default or specific config — a risk toggle the vendor already warns about is not "specific config".

full.label: Full mode
full.hint: Beyond high-impact bugs, also records hard-to-exploit items that still demonstrate a real difference (CORS, reflected XSS, missing rate limiting, security headers, plain CSRF, etc.), tagged by the Reviewer as low-impact / hard to exploit.

custom.label: Custom mode
custom.short: Scope decided by a named prompt from Settings
custom.hint: Vulnerability scope is decided entirely by the selected custom prompt (snapshotted into the project), with no bounty-mode hard gate in code. Create a custom audit mode in Settings first.

web.label: Web app
web.hint: Audited as a deployable application: HTTP plus WebSocket / RPC / MQ entry points are treated as sources.

library.label: Library
library.hint: Audited as a component: public APIs / parsers are the caller-controlled entry points. Defaults to local verification with the Verifier off at creation.

mixed.label: Mixed
mixed.hint: Prioritizes the library core; demo/sample/examples are down-weighted. Defaults to local verification with the Verifier off at creation.

exposureModeTooltip.indirectProven:
Indirect consumer: the component has no direct HTTP/RPC entry point, so it cannot be exploited by sending requests to it alone.
Full exploitation depends on an upstream application passing attacker input into the sink (e.g. a SELECT injection point via WallFilter).
The full upstream→component exploit chain has been proven at a real business HTTP/API entry point.
See "### Trigger conditions" in the report for details.
exposureModeTooltip.indirectUnproven:
Indirect consumer: the component has no direct HTTP/RPC entry point, so it cannot be exploited by sending requests to it alone.
Full exploitation depends on an upstream application passing attacker input into the sink (e.g. a SELECT injection point via WallFilter).
The full upstream chain has not been proven at a real business entry point; a harness or unit test calling the component API directly does not count.
Scoring and value tiering already reflect the indirect-consumer constraint (usually lower than a directly remotely exploitable web bug).
See "### Trigger conditions" in the report for details.
exposureModeTooltip.direct: Direct exposure: an attacker can reach the vulnerable sink directly through a user-controlled entry point (HTTP/RPC, etc.), without relying on an upstream application to pass input.

harnessTier.l1: L1: local verification (sink level). A mock harness calls the vulnerable sink function directly to prove the root cause is exploitable — no lab environment needed.
harnessTier.l2: L2: local verification (module level). A mock harness calls module-level functions, covering multiple paths — deeper than L1.
harnessTier.l3: L3: integration verification. Starts the service in a sandbox and runs poc.py to verify the full entry→sink path — equivalent to a live lab test.

fmt.auditModeCustomHint: Vulnerability scope currently follows the project's snapshot of custom mode "{{name}}"; no bounty hard gate. Takes effect on the next round after resuming.

auditModeSelect.addCustomFirst: Add a custom audit mode in Settings first.

bountyScope.title: Bounty mode scope
bountyScope.description: Only records issues that are exploitable by default and cause real impact. Full reference below.
bountyScope.premise: Exploitation must hold under the default config, or by changing only the application's own config options. Mark each submission as default or specific config; a risk toggle the vendor already warns about is not "specific config". Planting files, changing non-application config, or chaining a second independent bug are not allowed. Full mode additionally records items from the "not recorded" list above that still demonstrate a real difference, tagged by the Reviewer as low-impact / hard to exploit.

file_op.note: Read / write / delete / modify / copy / archive traversal, etc.

ssrf_internal.note: Internal network, cloud metadata, or sensitive local ports

stored_xss.note: Must be persisted and execute in another user's browser; do not label reflected XSS as stored

csrf_1click.note: Victim opens a malicious page and immediately triggers RCE or another high-impact action; do not label plain CSRF (profile edits, logout) as 1-click

hardcoded_secret.note: Must be a server-side secret: JWT/HMAC signing, API signing secret, private key, third-party API key, ciphertext inside a protected store/backup, etc.; must enable unauthorized impact

other_impact.note: Must demonstrate code execution, sensitive data disclosure, unauthorized read/write/delete, or arbitrary file operations

ssrf_public.note: Cannot reach internal network / metadata / sensitive local ports

plain_csrf.type: Plain CSRF / just missing a token
plain_csrf.note: Low-impact state changes such as renaming, logout, likes, posts; or requires multiple clicks / confirmation

cors_headers.note: Includes ACAO reflection, CSP, X-Frame-Options, etc.

open_redirect.note: Unless it can be escalated to auth hijack, token theft, or other real impact

rate_limit.type: Missing rate limit / captcha brute force

weak_random.note: Unless it directly causes an auth bypass

frontend_aes.note: Key is in front-end JS or deliberately shipped publicly; decrypting a field the front end already decrypts / an intercepted login packet is not a CVE

config_default_password.type: Default password in a config file
config_default_password.note: User-changeable passwords or keys in application.yml, .env, compose, docs
